$schema: Canonical design tokens for Meridian's three frontend surfaces (Insights, Care, Family). This file is the single source of truth. Next.js consumes it via lib/tokens.ts + globals.css CSS vars (hand-mirrored, see file header there). SwiftUI (Care, Family) consumes it via DesignSystem/Tokens.swift in each app (hand-mirrored, same values). If you change a value here, update all three mirrors in the same commit.

color._assumption_warning: Base spec defines primary/primary-alt/success/destructive/background/foreground/muted/border but not a 'warning' token, even though IncidentSeverity has an 'info'/'warning'/'critical' three-tier scale distinct from the reserved destructive=emergency red. Added #B45309 (amber-700, 4.5:1+ on both background tones) for the 'warning' severity tier only. destructive (#DC2626) stays reserved exclusively for 'critical'/emergency per the hard constraint. 'info' severity uses foreground/primary tones, not a dedicated color, since it's not alert-worthy.

demoSkeleton.note: Intentional one-off palette for the standalone pitch-demo skeleton screen only (spec section 5) — never used elsewhere.

contrast.target: AAA where feasible for large text and alert states

typography.heading: Figtree
typography.monoUsage: Insights dense/raw-data tables only (timestamps, IDs, raw values) — nowhere else, and never on Care or Family.
typography.iosNote: Figtree/Noto Sans aren't practical to bundle reliably across two SwiftUI app targets on this timeline; iOS surfaces use San Francisco (system font) at Figtree-equivalent weights (.semibold/.bold for headings, .regular/.medium for body) to match the same 'medical, clean, accessible, trustworthy' mood rather than the literal font file.

motion.alertArrival: single one-time scale/pop-in on arrival, then hold steady until acknowledged — never continuous flashing or pulsing

touchTarget.note: Critical severity issue if violated on Care — a mis-tap on the wrong resident's resolve button during a real emergency is a real failure mode.

iconography.rule: No emoji as icons anywhere, including severity/status icons.
